issues.legal_issue: A liquidator must provide reasons when rejecting the highest bid in a liquidation auction, including for auctions conducted before the requirement was expressly added to the regulations.
A liquidator cannot cancel an otherwise valid auction solely in the hope of obtaining a higher price, and has no unfettered discretion to do so.

A highest bidder does not acquire an indefeasible right to acceptance of its bid before the sale is completed, but the bid should ordinarily be accepted absent statutory infirmity, collusion, or fraud.

A former director or promoter’s past relationship with a corporate debtor does not, without a continuing connection to its business, make an auction purchaser ineligible as a related party under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
A financial creditor with a substantial interest in the liquidation auction may appeal an order of the adjudicating authority concerning that auction.
